question: Sand falls at the rate of $36\pi$ cm$^3$/s and forms a conical heap whose radius is always twice its height. Find the rate at which the height increases when the heap is $3$ cm high.
explanation: Geometrical relationLet $h$ be the height and $r$ be the radius. Since $r=2h$, the volume is$$V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\frac{1}{3}\pi(2h)^2h=\frac{4}{3}\pi h^3$$Differentiation with respect to time$$\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi h^2\frac{dh}{dt}$$Substitution of the given valuesAt $h=3$ cm and $\frac{dV}{dt}=36\pi$ cm$^3$/s,$$36\pi=4\pi(3)^2\frac{dh}{dt}$$Simplification$$36\pi=36\pi\frac{dh}{dt}\Rightarrow\frac{dh}{dt}=1$$Final resultThe height of the conical heap is increasing at $1$ cm/s.
